sourceObservations.observation: Minimum-time heuristic uses travel at maximum possible speed; admissibility requires not overestimating actual time. Formula is derived from the printed principle.
Summary explicitly contrasts full-map offline global planning with real-time reactive local planning; grids/graphs are separate representations.
New sensor-detected obstacle unknown during global planning requires reaction or representation update; static-map route alone not permanently safe.

answers.reasoning: For any feasible route length L≥d and speed≤vmax, travel time≥L/vmax≥d/vmax. Distance divided by speed has time units; product, inverse quotient and bare distance do not. Easy conceptual classification now matches this one-law selection rather than overstating hard numerical reasoning.

The actual summary pairs full-map global planning with nearby reactive local planning; next lecture illustrates a new obstacle detected after prior static-map planning. Reversed scope and representation/objective-only distinctions are plausible confusions, not universal sensor denial or permanent-safety claims.
